article.title: GitHub - brumar/chess-postmortem-skills: Claude Code skills for chess post-mortems: Stockfish-backed annotated PGN, HTML viewer, narrated video

editorial:
A Tune-Up for Your Troubled Knights ♟️

A chess game is a little factory of decisions: each move inherits the workmanship of the last. This project puts Stockfish to work not merely stamping moves “good” or “bad,” but tracing where the assembly line went crooked. An annotated PGN makes the diagnosis portable; the viewer makes it approachable. 🔧

The cleverest part is inviting the player’s own account into the workshop. A recording transcribed locally, paired with clock times, can reveal whether a mistake came from a faulty plan or a ticking clock. That is useful instruction: repair the thinking process, and tomorrow’s moves may take care of themselves.

An hour of analysis is no bargain for every five-minute scramble. But for a serious game, a narrated video and questions about particular positions offer more than a shiny engine number. I would call that sound engineering: spend the time where the machine can be improved, not where it merely makes noise. 🚗

by Henry Ford
